symptoms.symptom: Surface units will not maintain a rolling boil or cooking is not fast enough

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use pans which are flat and match the diameter of the surface unit selected.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Improper cookware being used."

symptoms.symptom: Surface units do not work properly

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Cooktop controls improperly set.
remedies: Check to see the correct control is set for the surface unit you are using.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Cooktop controls improperly set."

symptoms.symptom: Scratches (may appear as cracks) on cooktop glass surface

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
remedies: Scratches are not removable.
Tiny scratches will become less visible in time as a result of cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Incorrect cleaning methods being used."

causes.label: Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop.
remedies: To avoid scratches, use the recommended cleaning procedures.
Make sure bottoms of cookware are clean before use, and use cookware with smooth bottoms.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop."

causes.label: Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface."

symptoms.symptom: Areas of discoloration on the cooktop

causes.label: Food spillovers not cleaned before next use.
remedies: See the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Food spillovers not cleaned before next use."

causes.label: Hot surface on a model with a light-colored cooktop.
remedies: This is normal.
The surface may appear discolored when it is hot.
This is temporary and will disappear as the glass cools.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Hot surface on a model with a light-colored cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Plastic melted to the surface

causes.label: Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop.
remedies: See the Glass surface—potential for permanent damage section in the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Pitting (or indentation) of the cooktop

causes.label: Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop.
remedies: Call a qualified technician for replacement.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Frequent cycling off and on of surface units

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use only flat cookware to minimize cycling.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 48: "Improper cookware being used."

symptoms.symptom: Food does not speed bake properly

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.

causes.label: Rack position is incorrect or the rack is not level.

causes.label: Incorrect use of cookware and/or aluminum foil.

causes.label: Cookware of improper size being used.

causes.label: Door not closed.

causes.label: Very delicate item.

causes.label: Food not to desired doneness.
remedies: Cook times will vary due to recipe and pan variations.
Check food when prompted and add additional time with More Time if needed.

causes.label: Sauce on food gets too brown.
remedies: Apply sauce later in cooking cycle.

causes.label: Meat cooked too long.

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.

causes.label: Improper rack position being used.

symptoms.symptom: Cook time doesn’t countdown while speedcooking

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See Using the Trivection™ Oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 49: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: Door is not closed completely.
remedies: Close door completely.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 49: "Door is not closed completely."

causes.label: START not selected.

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 49: "START not selected."

symptoms.symptom: Option not seen on the display screen

remedies: Select MORE to see additional items.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Option may be listed on the next screen."

symptoms.symptom: Hot air from oven

causes.label: When using the cooking features, hot air will exit the oven through the vent located above the door.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "When using the cooking features, hot air will exit the oven through the vent located above the door."

symptoms.symptom: Food does not bake or roast properly in the oven

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using traditional bake and roast section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: Shelf position is incorrect or the shelf is not level.
remedies: See the Using traditional bake and roast section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Shelf position is incorrect or the shelf is not level."

causes.label: Incorrect cookware or cookware of improper size being used.
remedies: See the Using traditional bake and roast section.

remedies: See the Adjust the oven temperature—Do it yourself! section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Oven temperature needs adjustment."

symptoms.symptom: Food does not broil properly

remedies: Make sure you select BROIL.

remedies: See the Broiling Guide.

remedies: For best results, use a pan designed for broiling.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Cookware not suited for broiling."

symptoms.symptom: Clock and timer do not work or display goes blank

remedies: See the Using the clock and lower oven timer section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "Controls improperly set."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 50: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

symptoms.symptom: Oven temperature too hot or too cold

causes.label: Oven temperature needs adjustment.
remedies: See the Adjust the oven temperature—Do it yourself! section.

symptoms.symptom: Oven will not work

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

symptoms.symptom: “Crackling” or “popping” sound in the oven

causes.label: This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions."

symptoms.symptom: Excessive smoking in the oven during a clean cycle

causes.label: Excessive soil.
remedies: Press the CLEAR/OFF pad.
Open the windows to rid the room of smoke.
Wait until the    (LOCK) light goes off.
Wipe up the excess soil and reset the clean cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Excessive soil."

symptoms.symptom: Oven door will not open after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven too hot.
remedies: Allow the oven to cool below locking temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Oven too hot."

symptoms.symptom: Oven not clean after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: Oven was heavily soiled.
remedies: Clean up heavy spillovers before starting the clean cycle.
Heavily soiled ovens may need to self-clean again or for a longer period of time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "Oven was heavily soiled."

symptoms.symptom: Display shows "ERR"

causes.label: A temperature was set outside the allowable range of 170°F–550°F.
remedies: Set the temperature between 170°F–550°F.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 51: "A temperature was set outside the allowable range of 170°F–550°F."

symptoms.symptom: “F— and a number or letter” flash in the oven display

causes.label: You have a function error code.
remedies: Press the CLEAR/OFF pad.
Allow the oven to cool for one hour.
Put the oven back into operation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "You have a function error code."

causes.label: If the function code repeats.
remedies: Disconnect all power to the cooking center for at least 30 seconds and then reconnect power.
If the function error code repeats, call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "If the function code repeats."

symptoms.symptom: Power outage, clock flashes

causes.label: Power outage or surge.
remedies: Reset the clock.
If the oven was in use, you must reset it by pressing the CLEAR/OFF pad, setting the clock and resetting any cooking function.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Power outage or surge."

symptoms.symptom: “Burning” or “oily” odor emitting from oven vent

causes.label: This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time.
remedies: To speed the process, set a self-clean cycle for a minimum of 3 hours.
See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time."

symptoms.symptom: Strong odor in the oven

causes.label: An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used.
remedies: This is temporary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used."

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 52: "Rear drawer support is on top of the guide rail."

symptoms.symptom: Storage drawer won’t close

remedies: Reposition the drawer and power cord.
